status: exploratory amendment fixed after the owner's session-order correction, before time-adjusted fits
time: Use the original unique, session-wide trial_index across BOTH interventions. u=(trial_index-1)/(planned_trials-1)-.5; do not restart at intervention change. The observed release has indices 1-204 and 205-408 in the two parts. This is recorded trial order, not verified elapsed clock time.
interpretation: Early blocks of the second intervention occur later in the same session. Early-block fits remain smaller-trial sensitivities and cannot exclude fatigue. Main adjustment uses all retained trials.
primary: Shared additive participant-specific global linear RT trend gamma_i*u in both AT and Baseline likelihoods, jointly fitted with four PPS curves and Baseline uncertainty. gamma_i=beta_time+tau_time*z_i; beta_time Normal(0,.2 seconds), tau_time HalfNormal(.15), z_i Normal(0,1). Allow speeding or slowing; no negative-slope constraint.
sensitivity: Add a shared quadratic term gamma2_i*u^2 with the same proper coefficient priors. All coefficients and PPS uncertainty stay joint; no plug-in detrending or renewed exclusion based on the fitted trend.
fits: Five additional full-session fits: linear raw/rolling x broad/visible95, plus quadratic raw broad. Same original+local filtering, positive-amplitude nuisance priors, shape priors, 40-person cohort, units and contrasts as the preceding trial-cleaning specification.
likelihood: Exact Gaussian within-distance sufficient statistics include RT-time cross-products and time-feature cross-products. Residualize conditionally on sampled trend coefficients inside the likelihood, not by fixing a preliminary slope. For rolling candidates apply H and the full overlap covariance after this symbolic adjustment. Baseline and AT times remain distinct and uncertainty propagates jointly.
estimand: PPS corrected curves at the common centered session reference u=0. Shared RT drift cancels in the ideal same-time AT-minus-Baseline expectation. Include observed differences in trial timing when fitting and predicting; do not describe average RT drift as a boundary effect.
sampling: Four nutpie chains, 2000 tuning/2000 draws at target .99; once 4000/4000 only for failed convergence. Same zero-divergence, Rhat<=1.01 and bulk/tail ESS>=400 full-model gate. Retain all failures.
validation: Five additional held-distance linear/raw/broad refits. Learn both RT filters without held AT outcomes; retain independent Baseline calibration and original global trial-time coordinates. Score the same initially eligible raw targets as the preceding fifteen folds, using each target's actual recorded trial order. Predictive 1000/1000, once 3000 draws/2000 tune if needed; identical gates.
limits: Counterbalanced intervention order is retained (20 per sequence). A shared additive time trend controls a specified RT-level nuisance process; it does not identify fatigue causally or exclude carryover, stimulus changes, condition-dependent time trends or dynamic PPS changes. No timing exclusion, negative trend, effect significance, or gain in R2 is guaranteed. Broader recovery/coverage and reduced-shape-model goals remain open.
